subject.title: Memory system: Cannot delete stale memories, conflicting entries persist

question: Should memory_recall expose stable deletable UUIDs in model-visible content now, or should this wait for a broader Memory MVP lifecycle contract with replacement, tombstone, and conflict-resolution semantics?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the supported user-facing memory API affects deletion safety, durable IDs, conflict semantics, and future plugin compatibility, so automation should not choose the contract alone.

options.title: Expose recall UUIDs narrowly
options.body: Add full UUIDs to memory_recall content with regression and live plugin proof, while explicitly leaving replacement and tombstone semantics to the broader Memory MVP trackers.

options.title: Design lifecycle contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers settle the canonical memory schema, supersede/tombstone states, and conflict-resolution flows before changing recall output.

options.title: Use a non-UUID deletion handle
options.body: Define an opaque model-visible deletion selector instead of raw UUIDs, accepting extra API design work before implementation.

recommendation.title: Expose recall UUIDs narrowly
recommendation.body: Add full UUIDs to memory_recall content with regression and live plugin proof, while explicitly leaving replacement and tombstone semantics to the broader Memory MVP trackers.
